slides.title: Shape Operators As Normal Turning
slides.notes: Start by framing the chapter as the study of how a surface normal changes when the base point moves. The first important distinction is that the metric on the surface sees lengths and angles, while the shape operator records how the surface sits in three-dimensional space. Tell students that every later formula is a way to measure this turning more economically.

slides.title: The Data At One Surface Point
slides.notes: Use this slide to fix the pieces of data before any formula appears. A point on a patch has two tangent directions and a chosen unit normal, and the derivative of that normal along tangent directions is again tangent. Emphasize that the operator is local: it is built at one point, but it predicts directional bending through every tangent direction there.

slides.title: Definition: The Shape Operator
slides.notes: Present the definition as a sign convention plus a geometric act. Move in a tangent direction, watch the unit normal move on the unit sphere, then pull that derivative back as tangent information. The minus sign is not mystical; it aligns the sphere with positive principal curvatures for the outward normal convention used in many computations.

slides.title: Normal Curvature Samples One Direction
slides.notes: Now reduce the operator to a scalar in one tangent direction. The normal curvature is the inner product of the shape operator applied to a unit direction with that same direction. Point out that the same point can bend differently in different tangent directions, which is the first reason a single curvature number is usually not enough.

slides.title: Principal Directions Diagonalize The Reading
slides.notes: Connect the extremal normal curvatures to a symmetric linear operator on the tangent plane. Principal directions are the axes where the mixed part disappears and the normal curvature reading becomes an eigenvalue. The diagram should be read as a tangent-plane instrument, not as a literal flattening of the surface.

slides.title: Euler Formula Is A Curvature Dial
slides.notes: Use the formula as the payoff for diagonalizing the shape operator. Once the two principal curvatures are known, every normal curvature value is a weighted blend determined by the angle from a principal direction. This is a good moment to ask students what information is lost if they only remember the Gaussian curvature.

slides.title: Gaussian And Mean Curvature
slides.notes: Distinguish the two standard summaries of the shape operator. Gaussian curvature is the determinant and controls the product of the two principal bendings, while mean curvature is half the trace and records their average signed bending. The pair is compact, but the full operator still remembers the principal directions.

slides.title: Three Local Shapes, Three Signs
slides.notes: Use the sign of Gaussian curvature as a visual classifier. Positive curvature bends the same way in all tangent directions, negative curvature bends oppositely across two principal axes, and zero curvature indicates at least one direction with no normal bending. Stress that this is local classification, not a global description of the whole surface.

slides.title: Computing From The First And Second Forms
slides.notes: This is the computational bridge from patch data to the operator. The first fundamental form measures tangent inner products, and the second fundamental form measures normal acceleration. In coordinates, the shape operator is obtained by raising one index with the metric matrix, so the formula depends on coordinates while the resulting linear map does not.

slides.title: Implicit Surfaces Need A Different Entry Point
slides.notes: For a level surface, the gradient supplies the normal direction without a parametric patch. The Hessian then tells how the gradient changes along tangent directions, giving the same curvature information after projection and normalization. This route is especially useful for spheres, quadrics, and numerically sampled surfaces where a patch may be inconvenient.

slides.title: Special Curves Detect The Operator
slides.notes: Move from pointwise directions to curves whose tangents follow geometrically meaningful directions. Lines of curvature follow principal directions, so the shape operator does not rotate their tangent direction into another tangent axis. Asymptotic directions, when they exist, have zero normal curvature and therefore expose the saddle behavior of negative Gaussian curvature.

slides.title: Surfaces Of Revolution Split The Work
slides.notes: Use revolution surfaces because their symmetry makes the principal directions visible before computation. One principal direction follows the meridian curve and the other follows the circular parallel. The two curvatures then answer different questions: how the profile curve bends, and how the normal turns while the point moves around the axis.

slides.title: A Ruled Surface Can Hide Zero Curvature
slides.notes: Present this as a warning against reading every curved-looking surface as having nonzero Gaussian curvature. Cylinders and other developable examples can bend in space while preserving one zero principal curvature. The shape operator sees that one tangent direction carries no normal bending, which is exactly what a flat sheet can do when rolled.

slides.title: Sign Conventions Are Testable
slides.notes: Make the normal orientation issue explicit. Reversing the chosen unit normal reverses the shape operator and the principal curvatures, but Gaussian curvature stays the same because it is a product of two signs. This is the kind of convention that should be caught by a model check rather than memorized as a slogan.

slides.title: Notebook Lab: From Picture To Residual
slides.notes: Connect the lecture back to the chapter notebook. The visual artifacts are not decoration; each one names the invariant or residual that the reader should inspect. Encourage students to rerun a model after changing a parameter and to ask whether a failing check indicates a mathematical assumption, a sign convention, or a genuine implementation error.

slides.title: What To Carry Forward
slides.notes: Close by compressing the chapter into a working habit. The shape operator turns normal variation into a tangent-plane linear map, normal curvature samples it, principal curvatures diagonalize it, and Gaussian and mean curvature summarize it. The next stage of differential geometry keeps using this pattern: define local data, test its invariance, and read geometric meaning from controlled examples.
